topics.topic: Filesystem identity and containment rules for store and backup locations
questions: How are sameness and containment determined in the presence of relative paths, symlinks, bind mounts, hard links or path aliases?
What filesystem identity and containment check must Registry use to accept or refuse the configured locations?
By what filesystem identity and containment rules are equality and nesting checked?

quotes:
The store and the
   backup location are different places, neither inside the other; a
   configuration where they are the same or one holds the other fails the
   start.
judgement.divergence: One implementation compares normalized path strings and may accept symlinked, hard-linked or bind-mounted aliases; another resolves filesystem identity and containment and refuses them. The owner notices whether Registry starts with a store and backups that physically overlap.
judgement.why: The exact refusal condition depends on an unspecified filesystem identity and containment rule.

topics.topic: Interaction between post-import and ordinary daily backups
questions: Does a successful post-import backup count as that UTC day's daily backup and suppress the scheduled or catch-up backup, or may both be kept on the same day?
Does an import-triggered backup count as the day's backup and suppress the ordinary 03:00 or startup run, or may both an import backup and one ordinary daily backup be kept that day?
Does a successful post-import backup count as that day's daily backup, and does an already completed daily backup suppress or coexist with the post-import run?

quotes: Besides the run after an accepted import (A16), at most one backup is kept per UTC day, the kept backups themselves saying which days have one, and runs never overlap.

A run that 03:00 found Registry stopped is made when it next starts with its service tokens, if no backup was made that UTC
   day; an owner-only start makes no run (rule 10).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats the import-triggered backup as the day's backup and suppresses an ordinary or catch-up run; another treats it as an additional backup and still keeps one ordinary daily backup. The owner notices the number and timing of kept recovery points.
judgement.why: The exception permits an additional import run but does not say whether that run satisfies the separate daily-backup condition.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie scope, attributes, and HTTP behavior
questions: Which cookie attributes and scope enforce this rule, especially since cookies are scoped by host/domain and path rather than by full origin?
What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “only to Registry's own origin,” including access on the Registry host without HTTPS?
What exact cookie scope and attributes are required, and may a session cookie be sent over same-machine HTTP?

judgement.why: This is the same owner-session cookie attributes, scope and transport question already assigned to State 6, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes, scope, and HTTP transport rules
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Authenticated-encryption format and authenticated metadata for backups
questions: Which authenticated-encryption format, algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation and versioning rules define a valid encrypted backup?
What authenticated-encryption format is required, and which metadata must be cryptographically authenticated?

judgement.why: This is the same authenticated backup-encryption and envelope-format question already assigned to State 6, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Interoperable authenticated-encryption and envelope format for backups
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Import-file digest algorithm, input representation, comparison, and collisions
questions: Which digest algorithm is used, and is it calculated over the exact uploaded bytes or over a canonical parsed representation?
How is the import file digest computed and compared, and what happens if two different uploaded byte sequences have the same digest?

judgement.why: This is the same import-file digest algorithm, representation and collision question already assigned to State 6, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Import-file digest algorithm, input representation, and collision handling
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Post-import backup timing, completion reporting, and retry obligations
questions: How does the owner learn that a checked backup containing the import exists, and does the import response wait for that check or return as soon as the import transaction commits?
When does the import-triggered backup run relative to the import response, and how is its retry obligation scheduled and persisted?

quotes:
Right after an accepted import Registry makes a backup run outside the
   daily schedule (A18), so the import reaches a checked backup as soon as it
   can; a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays
   accepted.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving. Whether the runs succeed is the
   owner's to watch on the host (Explicit exclusions: the host's
   administration).

A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again: the owner
keeps the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import
until a checked backup holds the import, and retires the VPS instance only
then (R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation blocks the import response until the post-import backup is checked and reports failure directly; another returns immediately after the import transaction and performs or retries the backup asynchronously through ordinary runs. The owner notices when the import completes and when it is safe to retire the VPS source.
judgement.why: The texts require the run and host diagnostics but do not settle its ordering relative to the import response or how the owner identifies completion of the required checked backup.

topics.topic: Representation, storage, and comparison of confirmation-bound values
questions: How are the submitted target and inputs compared with those bound to the confirmation: exact encoded values, normalized domain values, or a canonical digest?
Does the pending confirmation store those personal values, or only a non-reversible binding to values resubmitted with the confirmation?

quotes: | `business_confidential` | every other fact of every model: `project_id`, alias, status, revision, instants, the archived and anonymised marks; `customer_ref`, the Customer's kind, revision, instants and its erased, restricted and ended marks with their dates; `room_id`, room name and added instant; every artifact pointer fact; every agent session fact and the access request's text; every audit entry; the migration closure; the owner session, but for its uploaded import file |

changed by the owner's requests (State 2 A13, A16; owner,
2026-10-31): the instant of its last request, which starts as the instant it
began; at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its
target, the revision or access version and the inputs it is bound to, and
the instant it was shown — made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced
by the next one shown and cleared when used; and at most one uploaded import
file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks.

the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation stores and compares the raw submitted names, aliases and Customer values; another stores a canonical or non-reversible binding and compares normalized domain values. The owner notices whether equivalent resubmissions are accepted, while the handling of personal data in the session also differs.
judgement.why: The texts require binding to the inputs but do not define the bound representation or equality rule, particularly for import values carrying personal data.

topics.topic: Short-circuiting versus aggregating ordered failures within a check stage
questions: Within a stage, does Registry stop at the first ordered failure or aggregate all failures, including checks that cannot safely or meaningfully run after an earlier failure?
Do owner-session, CSRF and confirmation checks short-circuit in their stated order, or are all stage-1 failures evaluated and returned together?

quotes:
Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF
   value, then a confirmation value where one is asked (A13);

When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of
   them.
judgement.why: The first failing stage supplies the answer, but all failures within that stage are named; the owner checks retain their stated evaluation order.

topics.topic: Whether a no-op audit erasure writes an erasure entry
questions: Must an accepted erasure that finds no qualifying entry append an erasure entry?
Does a confirmed erasure that matches no entries write an erasure audit entry and confirmation id?

quotes: every entry older than the date the owner gives is gone; the erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date (R0-66)

An erasure that removes no entry changes nothing: it is accepted, writes no
   entry and mints no confirmation id (A14).
judgement.why: State 0 requires the audit-erasure action to leave its own entry, while A15 expressly says an accepted no-op erasure leaves none.

topics.topic: Backup metadata value for a store with no audit entries
questions: What value is recorded and checked when the store has never written an audit entry?

topics.topic: Backup-key digest algorithm, representation, and collision handling
questions: Which digest algorithm and representation identify the key, and must collisions between configured or retained keys be detected?

topics.topic: Complete set of import values included in confirmation binding
questions: Must the confirmation value be bound directly to names, aliases and all Customer mapping values as well as to the file digest and picks?

topics.topic: Concurrency-safe updating of owner-session activity time
questions: How is last_request updated when several requests for one owner session overlap, so that a later-finishing older request cannot move the value backwards?

topics.topic: Configuration inputs inspected for unknown items
questions: Which inputs are inspected for unknown items—for example, a dedicated file or prefix, command-line options, or the process's entire environment?

topics.topic: Cutoff replay semantics for non-monotonic audit erasures after restore
questions: Which cutoff must be replayed when audit-erasure actions were performed with non-monotonic dates?

topics.topic: Distinguishing a first installation from loss of an existing store
questions: How does startup distinguish an intentional first installation from loss of an existing production store, so it does not silently serve a new empty production history?

topics.topic: Durable audit-history identity across restore and sequence reuse
questions: Since sequence numbers used after the backup may be reused in the restored history, does each store history need a durable identity in audit entries or backup metadata, or are entries identified only within whichever current history holds them?

topics.topic: Handling an expired pending confirmation after a mismatched submission
questions: If the pending confirmation has expired but the submission gives a different confirmation value, is the expired pending value cleared or retained?

topics.topic: Identifying Registry-owned files in the backup location
questions: How does Registry distinguish backups and temporary files it owns from unrelated, malformed or attacker-placed files in the configured backup location?

topics.topic: Import inputs retained until a checked backup permits recovery
questions: Which complete set of import mapping inputs must the owner retain until a checked backup holds the import, including the Customer values required by A16?

topics.topic: Mapping imported v1 project fields into embedded Object values
questions: What object values are shown and imported for each picked v1 project, and how are the v1 address and any other source fields mapped to the required embedded Object's address, kind and characteristics?

topics.topic: Pre-session request exemptions from owner-session and CSRF checks
questions: Is sign-in exempt from the owner-session and CSRF requirements, and if so, which other pre-session requests are exempt?

topics.topic: Representation measured for the minimum secret length
questions: For textual configuration values, which encoding or decoded representation is measured for the 32-byte requirement?

topics.topic: Request-id reuse after its original idempotency record is erased
questions: Is the same request id permanently tied to its original create, or may it create a second record after the original idempotency fact is erased?

topics.topic: Required scope of backup integrity checks
questions: What exact integrity check must run and pass: only the storage engine's structural check, or also Registry's domain invariants and foreign-reference checks?

topics.topic: Stage and short-circuit behavior of the agent project-membership check
questions: At which stage is project membership checked, and can any later validation run after membership fails?

topics.topic: Startup validity when all service tokens are absent
questions: Does a configuration with no Client Portal token start successfully when all four service tokens are absent?

topics.topic: Storage, isolation, and cleanup lifecycle of uploaded import files
questions: Where may the uploaded personal-data file be stored, and what cleanup and access-isolation rules apply on normal expiry, replacement, crash and restart?

topics.topic: Timestamp sampling and equality within an atomic change
questions: At what point is now sampled for an atomic change, and must the record's last-changed instant, lifecycle instant and audit-entry instant for one action be identical?

topics.topic: Whether import validation covers the whole file or only selected records
questions: Are malformed records and production conflicts reported for the whole file or only for the picked projects and records they bring in?

topics.topic: Whether retention continues after one backup deletion fails
questions: After one expired backup cannot be deleted, must Registry continue attempting the other expired backups and the rest of the run?

topics.topic: Whether startup catch-up backup blocks request serving
questions: Must a service-enabled startup complete the due backup run before serving requests, or may it begin serving while the run proceeds?
